title: C++ Constants and Literals
description: Constants and literal syntax in C++: const versus constexpr, #define, integer, floating, character, string and boolean literals, suffixes, escape sequences and const correctness.

descriptionI18n.zh-Hant: C++ 的常數與字面值語法：const 與 constexpr 的差別、#define、整數／浮點／字元／字串／布林字面值、後綴、跳脫序列與 const 正確性。

questions.prompt: Why is `constexpr int MAX = 100;` generally preferred over `#define MAX 100`?

prompt.zh-Hant: 為何 `constexpr int MAX = 100;` 通常比 `#define MAX 100` 更好？

a.zh-Hant: 它具有型別、遵守作用域規則，並由編譯器檢查。

b.zh-Hant: 它比較快，因為會被前置處理器替換。

c.zh-Hant: 它可以在執行時視需要修改。

d.zh-Hant: 它保證常數不佔用任何記憶體。

explanation.zh-Hant: `constexpr` 建立真正有型別、有作用域的實體，編譯器能檢查轉型，除錯器也看得到。`#define` 只是編譯前的文字替換，沒有型別也沒有作用域，還可能因運算子優先順序而出錯。

options.text: It has a type, obeys scope rules and is checked by the compiler.
It is faster because it is replaced by the preprocessor.
It can be modified at run time when needed.
It guarantees that no memory is used for the constant.

questions.explanation: `constexpr` creates a real, typed, scoped entity, so the compiler can check conversions and the debugger can see it. `#define` is a textual substitution performed before compilation, with no type and no scope, and it is prone to operator-precedence surprises.

questions.prompt: What is the type of the literal `42u`?

prompt.zh-Hant: 字面值 `42u` 的型別是甚麼？

explanation.zh-Hant: `u` 或 `U` 後綴讓整數字面值成為無號型別，因此 `42u` 的型別是 `unsigned int`；若加上 `ull` 才會是 `unsigned long long`。

questions.explanation: The `u`/`U` suffix makes an integer literal unsigned, so `42u` has type `unsigned int`. Adding `ull` would make it `unsigned long long`.

questions.prompt: How many characters does the string literal "a\tb" contain, not counting the terminating null?

prompt.zh-Hant: 字串字面值 "a\tb" 含有幾個字元（不計結尾的空字元）？

explanation.zh-Hant: 跳脫序列 `\t` 代表一個定位字元（tab），所以字串內容是 `a`、一個 tab、`b`，共三個字元，再加上結尾的空字元。

questions.explanation: The escape sequence `\t` stands for a single tab character, so the literal holds `a`, a tab and `b` — three characters, plus the null terminator.

questions.prompt: What is the main reason to replace a raw `86400` in code with `constexpr int kSecondsPerDay = 86400;`?

prompt.zh-Hant: 把程式中的 `86400` 換成具名常數 `constexpr int kSecondsPerDay = 86400;`，主要理由為何？

a.zh-Hant: 名稱說明了意義，而且只需在一處修改數值。

b.zh-Hant: 具名常數的執行速度比數字字面值快。

c.zh-Hant: 編譯器無法解析運算式中的數字字面值。

d.zh-Hant: 具名常數讓變數不需要宣告型別。

explanation.zh-Hant: 魔術數字（magic number）讓程式難以理解，也難以修改；具名常數能表達意圖、集中管理數值，並賦予它型別。它不會讓程式變快，也不會免除型別宣告。

options.text: The name documents the meaning and there is a single place to change the value.
Named constants execute faster than literal numbers.
The compiler cannot parse numeric literals inside expressions.
A named constant removes the need to declare the variable's type.

questions.explanation: Named constants make intent readable and localise future changes, and they give the value a type. They do not make the code faster or remove the need for a type.

questions.prompt: Which of these literals are valid in C++17? Select all that apply.

prompt.zh-Hant: 下列哪些字面值在 C++17 中合法？可多選。

explanation.zh-Hant: `42u` 是無號整數、`3.14f` 是 `float`、`"hello"` 是字串字面值。`1.2.3` 不是單一字面值，會被拆成 `1.2` 與 `.3`，在該位置造成語法錯誤。

questions.explanation: `42u` is an unsigned int, `3.14f` a float and `"hello"` a string literal. `1.2.3` is not one literal: it is parsed as `1.2` followed by `.3`, which is a syntax error in that position.

questions.prompt: Which statements about const correctness are true? Select all that apply.

prompt.zh-Hant: 關於 const 正確性（const correctness），下列敘述何者正確？可多選。

a.zh-Hant: `const` 成員函式不得修改非 `mutable` 的資料成員。

b.zh-Hant: `const T&` 參數可避免複製，並禁止透過該參考修改。

c.zh-Hant: 把 `const` 轉型去掉後再寫入一定是安全的。

d.zh-Hant: 指向 const 的指標（`const int*`）可以指向非 const 物件。

explanation.zh-Hant: 成員函式加上 `const` 後，`this` 成為指向 const 的指標；`const T&` 不需複製且禁止寫入。只有物件原本就不是 const 時，去掉 const 再寫入才安全；若物件本身是 const，修改它是未定義行為。

options.text: A `const` member function may not modify non-`mutable` data members.
A `const T&` parameter avoids a copy and forbids modification through that reference.
Casting away `const` and writing through the result is always safe.
A pointer to const (`const int*`) may point at a non-const object.

questions.explanation: `const` on a member function makes `this` a pointer to const; `const T&` binds without copying and blocks writes. Casting away `const` is only safe if the object was not originally const — otherwise modifying it is undefined behaviour.

questions.prompt: A `constexpr` function can be called with run-time arguments, and that call is then evaluated at run time.

prompt.zh-Hant: `constexpr` 函式可以用執行期引數呼叫，此時該次呼叫會在執行期求值。

explanation.zh-Hant: `constexpr` 只表示「在引數為常數運算式時可在編譯期求值」；引數不是常數時，同一個函式照樣可以在執行期呼叫。

questions.explanation: `constexpr` means the function can be evaluated at compile time when its arguments are constant expressions. With run-time arguments the same function is simply called at run time.

questions.prompt: In C++, the string literal "hello" has type `const char[6]`.

prompt.zh-Hant: 在 C++ 中，字串字面值 "hello" 的型別是 `const char[6]`。

explanation.zh-Hant: 字串字面值是內含六個 `const char` 的陣列：五個字元加上結尾的空字元。C++11 起它是 const，直接寫入不符語法。

questions.explanation: The literal is an array of six `const char`: five characters plus the terminating null. It is const in C++11 and later, so writing to it is ill-formed.

questions.prompt: To make the literal `3.14` a `float` rather than a `double`, add the suffix ____.

prompt.zh-Hant: 若要讓字面值 `3.14` 成為 `float` 而非 `double`，需加上後綴 ____。

explanation.zh-Hant: 沒有後綴的浮點字面值型別是 `double`；`3.14f` 是 `float`，`3.14L` 則是 `long double`。

questions.explanation: An unsuffixed floating literal has type `double`; `3.14f` has type `float` and `3.14L` has type `long double`.

questions.prompt: Explain the difference between `const` and `constexpr`, and say when you would use each.

prompt.zh-Hant: 說明 `const` 與 `constexpr` 的差別，並各舉一個適用情境。

model.zh-Hant: `const` 承諾變數在初始化後不再改變，但初始值可以在執行期才算出來；`constexpr` 承諾在引數為常數時，數值或函式結果可以在編譯期求值，因此能用在陣列大小、樣板引數等常數運算式。編譯期常數用 `constexpr`，執行期才決定且不可變的值用 `const`。

explanation.zh-Hant: 關鍵差異是求值時機：`constexpr` 保證常數運算式，`const` 只保證不可修改。

answer.model: `const` promises that a value will not change after initialisation, but the initial value may be computed at run time. `constexpr` promises that the value or function result can be evaluated at compile time when its arguments are constant, so it can be used for array bounds, template arguments and other constant expressions. Use `constexpr` for compile-time constants and plain `const` for run-time values that must not change.

questions.explanation: The key difference is when the value is computed: `constexpr` guarantees a constant expression, while `const` only guarantees that the object is not modified.
